title: Stream + Tool RPC Patterns — SDK Ergonomics WIP
body:
Context:
We need a pragmatic pattern for calling external tools in the hosted streaming API that balances low-latency incremental text, typed structured results, and a simple SDK surface for client teams. Current prototypes focus on chunked frames and restartable sessions, but teams keep hitting UX friction around:
  - When to surface a tool call vs. inline text
  - How to represent partial structured outputs (valid JSON fragments vs typed frames)
  - Client backpressure and reconnection semantics when network drops mid-call
  - Observability for tool call latencies and per-frame billing

This doc is an exploratory sketch: not prescriptive yet. Goal: converge on a set of 2-3 RPC/handshake patterns we can ship/experiment with in the SDKs (JS + Python) and the hosted runtime.

Core ideas (high level):
1) Lightweight tool RPC over streaming frames:
   - Each stream is a sequence of typed frames: {meta, text, tool_request, tool_response, commit}
   - tool_request frame is an idempotent RPC invocation descriptor (tool id, args, call_id).
   - tool_response frames can be partial (progressive chunks) and end with a final commit frame.
   - The server can synthesize text frames referencing tool outputs (e.g., "[tool #42 summary]") or provide structured binding.

Pros: clear separation of concerns, replayable, works with incremental text. Cons: richer frame surface to teach SDKs.

2) Declarative action blocks with optimistic client hydration:
   - Model outputs a declarative action block (JSON schema reference) within text; SDK parses and exposes an Action object if it validates.
   - SDK can optionally trigger tool RPCs on behalf of the user with a single convenience API: session.triggerAction(action) which maps to the tool_request frame flow.

Pros: low cognitive overhead for app devs. Cons: requires reliable schema discovery and clear fallback when validation fails.

3) Prefetch + speculative-tool-call lane:
   - For common tool intents, SDK/server may speculatively call a cheap/low-risk tool and attach results as an additional channel.
   - If model later confirms need, the speculative result is instantly available (cache hit).

Operational considerations:
- Idempotency: every tool_request must include a stable call_id; server/runtime should dedupe repeated requests within a session window.
- Billing: track tool CPU/IO separately and map to call_id; when a speculative call is discarded, mark as billed but with a special tag. Need product decision.
- Privacy/PII: tool_request payloads can be large (docs/attachments). Default: redact sensitive tokens in telemetry; allow per-tenant opt-out.
- SLOs & fallback: if tool backend is slow, provide structured fallback signal to client (e.g., tool_response: {status: "degraded", partial: true, reason}).

SDK ergonomics (JS + Py):
- Primary surface: session.streamPrompt(prompt, {onFrame}) returns a session handle with:
    - onFrame(frame): called for every typed frame (text, meta, tool_request, tool_response, error)
    - handle.triggerTool(callDescriptor): convenience method that emits tool_request and returns a promise/yielding iterator of tool_response frames
    - handle.resumeFrom(snapshot): resume semantics for disconnected clients
- High-level helpers: session.getActions(callbacks) that returns validated Action objects and auto-wires triggerAction() to triggerTool under the hood.
- Backpressure: SDKs should expose an optional bufferLimit and onOverflow policy: drop-latest | block | raiseError. Default: buffer up to 32 frames then switch to sampling telemetry.

Telemetry / Observability:
- Emit a trace span per call_id with attributes: model_variant, route, call_type (tool/text), bytes_in, bytes_out, latency_first_byte, latency_completion.
- Add a per-frame metric for partial vs final frames to detect regressions where models never close commits.
- Add an "SDK-level sampled transcript" feature for debugging (PII controls).

Compatibility matrix (notes):
- Hosted runtime: must support frame routing, call dedup, speculative lane, and trace emission hooks.
- Dedicated: preserve same wire protocol but allow tenant-configurable speculative behavior.
- Private on-prem: disable speculative calls by default; provide an operator toggle.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Should tool_request be a first-class typed frame (explicit RPC) or embedded into a special mutable JSON token inside text? Explicit frame is clearer for replay but more complex on the wire.
- How do we enforce schema evolution for action blocks? Must version schemas and provide graceful downgrade paths.
- Billing semantics for speculative calls — charge always vs charge on-confirmation. Finance wants conservative approach (charge when executed), but that increases complexity.
- How far do we push convenience in SDKs vs. forcing explicit opt-in? Too much magic creates surprising costs.

Short checklist / next steps:
- [ ] Product decision on speculative billing (owners: Omar + Finance) — due 2025-03-07
- [ ] RFC for frame protocol draft (include sketches of JSON frames + stream lifecycle) — owner: Priya — draft by 2025-02-20
- [ ] Mini-experiment: JS SDK: implement handle.triggerTool() + onFrame sample, test with two toy tools (search + calculator) — owner: Hannah — spike by 2025-02-28
- [ ] Observability plan doc for per-call_id traces (SRE + Observability) — owner: Diego — draft by 2025-03-05

Notes to self / low-priority ideas:
- Consider a tiny on-wire compression for repeated frame metadata to reduce overhead for high-token streams.
- Investigate support for large binary attachments in tool_request via presigned URLs and progressive upload frames.
- UX: add a human-readable annotation for frames that are speculative vs confirmed so console logs are less noisy.

Slack threads / Cross refs:
- #hosted-api-streaming (thread id: 867), referenced prototype in GH PR 210.

If this reads sensibly, I will convert into a concise RFC with concrete wire examples and an initial JS SDK shim. Feedback welcome — tag me (priya) in the doc or drop comments inline.
